verdicts.tldr: every published $help page keeps the crawler's own 127.0.0.1 origin in its form action and its copy-link button
verdicts.details: Rendering the real HelpView (not a fixture) with Origin="http://127.0.0.1:8899" emits exactly two attributes carrying that origin, action= on the params form and data-copy-text-value= on the Link button, and neither is href or src. rewrite() at crawl.go:354 walks attrRe (crawl.go:40) which matches only href|src, so both survive verbatim; Seeds() adds u+"$help" for every realm at crawl.go:92, so every previewed realm ships one. A reviewer who presses Link on a published preview copies a loopback URL, and submitting the args form navigates to a refused connection. README.md:99 states "Every absolute URL is rewritten", which is false for these two. Fix: strip a leading c.Base (or any scheme+host) from the value before mapURL, and widen attrRe to the attributes gnoweb builds from Origin (action, data-copy-text-value).
verdicts.evidence: My own run against the real template, gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/components, go test -run TestHelpViewEmitsCrawlOriginOutsideHrefSrc -v: 'attribute carrying the crawl origin: data-copy-text-value="http://127.0.0.1:8899/r/gnoland/boards2/v0$help&func=CreateBoard&name="' and 'attribute carrying the crawl origin: action="http://127.0.0.1:8899/..."', origin-carrying attributes = action,data-copy-text-value, PASS. Rerunning the finder's artifact from the file: '--- FAIL: TestHelpPageKeepsCrawlerOrigin' with 'rewrite() left 2 reference(s) to the crawler's own gnodev (http://127.0.0.1:8899)', sibling '--- PASS: TestHrefIsRewrittenSoTheHarnessIsHonest'. Source: components/views/action.html:84 data-copy-text-value="{{ buildHelpURL $data . }}" and :104 action="{{ buildHelpURL $data . }}"; view_action.go:73 url.WriteString(data.Origin + pkgPath + "$help&func=" + fn.Name); handler_http.go:390 gnourl.Origin = requestOrigin(r); handler_http.go:933 host := r.Host; main.go:124 Base: fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d", cfg.port).
verdicts.verify_by: go test ./... -run TestHelpPageKeepsCrawlerOrigin -v in misc/gnopreview with the artifact test copied in: feed rewrite() the two attribute shapes action.html emits with the crawl origin expanded and count the surviving occurrences of http://127.0.0.1:8899; the sibling test pins that href= in the same body IS rewritten, so a failure is the attribute set and not the fixture

verdicts.tldr: the crawl-time gnodev host reaches the file on disk, not just the in-memory rewrite
verdicts.details: This candidate's check goes further than #190's: it runs the whole pipeline, Run() then Write(), and reads the written index.html. The crawl-time host is still in the file, so the defect is in the published artifact and not an artefact of calling rewrite() directly. attrRe at crawl.go:40 is the single cause, and mapURL would not help either, crawl.go:382 returns raw untouched for anything not starting with a single "/". Same user loss as #190, seen one layer later. Fix: same one place, strip the crawl origin before mapURL and cover action= and data-copy-text-value=.
verdicts.evidence: Rerunning the finder's artifact from the file, misc/gnopreview, go test -run TestSnapshotKeepsCrawlTimeOrigin -v ./...: '--- FAIL: TestSnapshotKeepsCrawlTimeOrigin', 'published snapshot still points at the crawl-time gnodev 127.0.0.1:38995', written page holding '<form class="params" method="GET" action="http://127.0.0.1:38995/r/x/y$help&func=Foo">' and '<button ... data-copy-text-value="http://127.0.0.1:38995/r/x/y$help&func=Foo">'; the sibling href on the same page did become ../../../../../r/x/y/_t/source/. The port differs from the finder's log (38995 here, 43095 there) because httptest picks it, which is what shows the run is mine. Independently: crawl.go:92 add(u + "$help") seeds one per realm, so no preview escapes it.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestSnapshotKeepsCrawlTimeOrigin ./... in misc/gnopreview with tests/b2-lines-r2-help-origin_test.go: crawl a $help body shaped like action.html against an httptest server, write the snapshot, assert the server host does not survive

verdicts.tldr: Crawler.order is a parallel key list nothing observes; deleting it is 3 lines out, 2 in
verdicts.details: I applied the rewrite myself: drop the order field, drop the append in Run, iterate slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(c.pages)) in writePages, add the maps import. git diff --stat reads '1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)', and the written tree is byte-identical, so crawl order is not observable in the output. The finder's second argument is weaker than it reads: main.go builds two separate Crawler values (c at :134, base at :271), so Run() is never called twice on one instance today and the stale-order nil-deref is latent, not reachable, which is why this stays a Suggestion. What the deletion buys is that c.order can no longer drift out of lockstep with c.pages, the way c.fileBudget already has. Fix: delete the field, the append and the range as in the attached patch.
verdicts.evidence: In my scratch worktree at ecf7af0f2: head run of the finder's artifact '--- PASS: TestWriteTreeIsOrderIndependent' with tree 'r/x/index.html d0799a7d, r/x/y/_a/p-about-e71ffeb2/index.html 38acdcd1, r/x/y/_t/help/index.html 74584614, r/x/y/_t/source/index.html ed963051, r/x/y/index.html 9208ff45'; after the rewrite the same five paths and the same five digests, go vet ./... silent, go test ./... 22/22 PASS, 'ok github.com/gnolang/gno/misc/gnopreview 0.006s', git diff --stat '1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)'. sortedKeys at plan.go:317 takes map[string]bool so it cannot be reused for map[string]*page, hence slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(...)).
